categoryName: Winter wear & thermals for a Himachal hill winter — jackets, sweaters, caps, gloves, mufflers, socks, shawls, thermal sets

skuLines.line: Men's thermal set (top + lower), cotton-blend mid-weight
skuLines.examples: Dollar Ultra Thermal Set, Lux Inferno, Amul Comfy/Ultima, Bodycare Insider
skuLines.packSizes: 1 set (top+lower); size 75-105 cm (S-XXL); pack-of-2 value packs
skuLines.seasonality: Sep-Nov build, peak Nov-Dec, dead after mid-Feb
skuLines.marginBand: 22-32% on MRP-fixed branded hosiery; 35-50% on unbranded Ludhiana hosiery
skuLines.notes: The single highest-volume line in the whole category. Buy on a size curve, not equal quantities — M/L/XL carry ~70% of demand. Keep in sealed poly with silica: Baru Sahib's Jul-Sep monsoon puts mildew on cotton knits held in an open godown.

skuLines.line: Men's thermal top only (full-sleeve, round/high neck)
skuLines.examples: Dollar Ultra Thermal Top, Lux Cozi, Lux Inferno, HAP
skuLines.notes: Tops sell roughly 2:1 against lowers — many men skip the lower. Stock tops deeper than sets and keep singles, not just sets, or you force a ₹700 purchase on a ₹300 need.

skuLines.line: Men's thermal lower / thermal trouser only
skuLines.examples: Dollar Ultra, Texfro woollen thermal bottom, Lux Inferno
skuLines.notes: Sold as a replacement/odd-size filler against sets. Waist sizing, so a shorter size ladder than tops.

skuLines.examples: Lux Cottswool, Lux Inferno Women, Dollar Ultra, Leading Lady, Kuchipoo
skuLines.notes: Must be stocked in skin/off-white and black. Under a salwar-kameez the thermal must not show at the neck — carry sleeveless and half-sleeve necklines alongside full-sleeve, which is the commonest miss in a male-buyer-led assortment.

skuLines.line: Women's thermal vest — sleeveless / half-sleeve, low neck
skuLines.examples: Lux Cottswool vest, Monte Carlo women thermal vest, Zeffit, Esoroucha
skuLines.notes: Worn under kameez/kurta all day; the neckline is the buying criterion, not warmth. Low-cut and sleeveless variants disappear first.

skuLines.line: Girls'/boys' junior thermal set (6-16 yrs, school sizes)
skuLines.examples: Monte Carlo girls thermal vest + lower, Lux Inferno kids, Dollar, HAP
skuLines.packSizes: 1 set per size; sizes 22"-40" chest / age 6-16
skuLines.seasonality: Sharp spike at Oct re-opening and again on return from winter break
skuLines.notes: Biggest single-cohort volume: ~2,000+ boarders who cannot go to town for a forgotten thermal. Hostel wardens buy in size sets — hold a pre-booked indent per house rather than guessing the curve. Two of each per child is the real norm (one on, one in wash) in a hostel with no daily laundry.

skuLines.line: Infant / toddler thermal suit, front-open button style
skuLines.examples: HF LUMEN button thermal suit, Kuchipoo vest+pyjama, Lux Inferno baby, HAP baby, Trampoline
skuLines.packSizes: set of top+pyjama; newborn-18M, 18M-4Y; packs of 2/3
skuLines.seasonality: Oct-Feb; babies need it 2-3 weeks earlier than adults
skuLines.notes: Front-open buttons, not pull-over-the-head — a mother of a 3-month-old will not buy a pull-on. Married-staff quarters make this a small but zero-substitute demand: nothing else on campus fits a baby.

skuLines.line: Premium merino / wool-blend heavy thermal set
skuLines.examples: Bhuttico merino base layer, Jockey thermals, Neva, Zero Degree merino
skuLines.notes: Thin, non-itchy, warmer per gram than cotton — the line for senior staff, anyone with a January night duty, and trekking students. Two sizes deep only; this is a demonstrated, sold-by-explanation item, not a self-service one.

skuLines.examples: Jockey thermal tee, Uniqlo HeatTech-alike, Van Heusen Innerwear, Zero Degree
skuLines.notes: The 2025-26 shift away from bulky waffle cotton. Sells to 18-25s who refuse to look like they are wearing a thermal — same warmth need, entirely different product.

skuLines.examples: Fleece-lined winter leggings, De Moza thermal leggings, local fleece jeggings
skuLines.notes: Fast-growing: worn under kurta/kameez in place of a thermal lower. Free-size dominates but stock XL/XXL — a plus-size gap is the commonest lost sale in women's winter bottoms.

skuLines.line: School-uniform pullover / sweater in school colours (V-neck, full sleeve)
skuLines.examples: Ludhiana uniform knitwear (made-to-colour), Duke/Monte Carlo school-grade acrylic pullover
skuLines.marginBand: 35-50% (better on a direct Ludhiana indent than through a distributor)
skuLines.notes: Colour is fixed by the Academy — this is an indent item ordered off a dye lot months ahead, not a shelf pick, and a colour mismatch between two lots is a complaint from every parent. Carry name-tape/embroidery as an attached service; boarders lose sweaters constantly.

skuLines.examples: Uniform acrylic cardigan, Monte Carlo half-cardigan, local knitwear
skuLines.notes: Preferred for younger children (5-10) who cannot manage a pull-over and for girls over a kameez. Buttons and cuffs are the failure points — check stitching on the indent sample before the lot ships up the hill; a return trip for a rejected lot is 30-50 km of road.

skuLines.examples: Half sweater, sleeveless uniform pullover, Duke half-sleeve sweater
skuLines.notes: The item that carries Oct and Mar, when a full sweater is too much. It also extends the selling season at both ends, which is exactly what reduces carry-over on a category that dies in March.

skuLines.line: Men's V-neck full-sleeve pullover (formal, over shirt)
skuLines.examples: Duke V-neck sweater (SDS series), Monte Carlo men pullover, Peter England
skuLines.notes: Teaching staff wear this over a shirt daily for four months. Navy, grey, black, maroon cover almost all of it — do not buy fashion colours into a 5,000-person closed campus where everyone sees everyone.

skuLines.line: Men's sleeveless V-neck cardigan / sweater vest
skuLines.examples: Monte Carlo men sleeveless V-neck cardigan, Duke, local wool blend
skuLines.notes: Works over a kurta and under a jacket, and does not fight a shoulder-worn dupatta or a shawl. High re-purchase among older male staff.

skuLines.examples: Duke half-zip & full-zip sweater, Monte Carlo high-neck, Monte Carlo stand-collar
skuLines.notes: A high neck replaces a muffler for a turbaned wearer, which matters here — a pull-on cap does not go over a dastaar but a zipped high collar does.

skuLines.line: Women's cardigan / long front-open woollen coatee
skuLines.examples: Monte Carlo women cardigan, Duke women front-open cardigan, local knit long cardigan
skuLines.notes: Longer lengths (hip/knee) outsell cropped in a modest-dress institution — a short cardigan over a kameez is not what women here buy. Keep it long, plain and dark.

skuLines.line: Women's woollen kurti / winter suit fabric (wool-blend salwar suit)
skuLines.examples: Bhuttico women's woollen suit, Monte Carlo winter kurti, local wool-blend suit piece
skuLines.packSizes: stitched kurti (S-XXL) or 2.5-3 m unstitched suit length
skuLines.seasonality: Oct-Dec (stitching lead time means women buy fabric early)
skuLines.notes: The genuinely local answer to cold for women here, and the line most retailers outside the hills skip entirely. Pair with the tailoring service — unstitched only sells if someone on campus can stitch it.

skuLines.examples: Duke Urban hooded sweatshirt, Monte Carlo Rock.it hoodie, Jockey French Terry hoodie
skuLines.seasonality: Sep-Feb, longest season of any line here
skuLines.notes: The default garment of an 18-25 campus, and the oversized fit is the 2026 shape. Highest fashion risk in the lane: buy plain and dark, keep prints shallow, and expect that whatever the students choose in October defines the rest of the season.

skuLines.examples: Duke round-neck sweatshirt, Monte Carlo Rock.it, Jockey pique sweatshirt, VCANEE/TRIPTEE mass
skuLines.notes: The value workhorse under ₹500 — carries staff, students and children alike. Fleece inside is the spec to insist on; plain cotton fleece-less sweatshirts do not hold at Baru Sahib's January mornings.

skuLines.examples: Monte Carlo boys/girls printed sweatshirt, Duke boys sweatshirt, mass hosiery prints
skuLines.notes: Non-uniform hours and Sunday wear. Small children's chest sizes move fastest and stock out first — the 22"-26" band is chronically under-bought.

skuLines.examples: Duke hooded tracksuit, Monte Carlo Rock.it tracksuit, Jockey fleece trackpants
skuLines.packSizes: set or separate lower; S-XXL, kids sizes
skuLines.notes: Doubles as school games kit and as hostel warm-wear. Fleece lower alone (₹250-500) is the volume item; sell the set to a smaller group.

skuLines.line: Fleece night suit / winter nightwear (women & kids)
skuLines.examples: DG Divine Girl fleece kurti+pyjama set, mass fleece night suits, Kuchipoo kids
skuLines.packSizes: set; free size, S-XXL; kids 2-12 yrs
skuLines.notes: Unheated hill quarters make night warmth a separate need from day warmth. Quietly one of the better-margin lines and almost never stocked by a general store.

skuLines.examples: Monte Carlo men puffer (detachable hood), Duke Urban puffer/bomber, Wildcraft, Woodland
skuLines.seasonality: Nov-Jan; one buy every 2-3 years per person
skuLines.notes: Highest ticket, highest markdown risk, and the purchase a resident would otherwise make on a trip to town — so it is the line that decides whether the wallet leaks off-campus. Keep the sharp end under ₹2,500 (GST on garments steps up above that threshold — confirm the current slab before pricing). Detachable hoods are the 2026 spec.

skuLines.line: Quilted / puffer jacket, women's longer length
skuLines.examples: Duke Urban women jacket, Monte Carlo women hooded jacket, Wildcraft women
skuLines.notes: Hip- or thigh-length only; a waist-length puffer over a salwar suit does not sell here. Under-served everywhere in small-town India — a real gap to hold depth in.

skuLines.examples: Monte Carlo boys & girls jacket, Duke boys jacket, mass hosiery kids jacket
skuLines.notes: Boarders' jackets get destroyed — stitching and zip quality drive complaints, not warmth. Hood must be attached, not detachable, for the under-10s who lose parts.

skuLines.line: Sleeveless quilted body warmer / half jacket
skuLines.examples: Duke sleeveless jacket, Monte Carlo hooded sleeveless jacket, mass quilted Alfa/Oswal body warmer
skuLines.notes: Warm core, free arms — worn over a kurta and under a shawl, which is exactly how older men here dress. Cheap, compact, no size drama, sells year after year.

skuLines.examples: Duke Urban reversible jacket (SDZ series), Monte Carlo reversible
skuLines.notes: A live 2026 line at Duke and Monte Carlo, and an easy sell on a closed campus where being seen in the same jacket daily matters. Two looks, one SKU — it also halves your colour-depth problem.

skuLines.examples: Duke Urban wind cheater, Wildcraft rain-shell, Decathlon Quechua
skuLines.seasonality: Two seasons: Jul-Sep monsoon and Nov-Feb wind/sleet
skuLines.notes: The only line here that sells in both of Baru Sahib's hard seasons, which makes it the lowest carry-over risk in the whole outerwear group. Wool over a wet monsoon walk is useless; a shell over a sweater is the local answer.

skuLines.examples: Jockey fleece full-zip high-neck jacket, Decathlon Quechua fleece, Duke fleece
skuLines.notes: Light, dries fast, machine-washable — better than wool in a damp hill hostel. Layers under the windcheater to replace a heavy jacket at half the ticket.

skuLines.line: Long coat / overcoat / pheran-style long woollen jacket
skuLines.examples: Bhuttico merino pheran, Monte Carlo long coat, Duke office-wear coat, Zero Degree wool coat
skuLines.marginBand: 25-35%, 20-30% if taken on consignment from a Kullu co-op
skuLines.notes: Slow, high-ticket, deep-winter only. Take it on consignment or against an order — do not own the inventory. Above ₹2,500 the GST slab also steps up, which is real money on a ₹5,000 coat.

skuLines.examples: Bhuttico merino half-sleeve Nehru jacket, Monte Carlo Nehru jacket, local wool waistcoat
skuLines.seasonality: Oct-Feb; spikes at Gurpurab and function dates
skuLines.notes: The correct formal winter layer over a kurta at a Sikh institution — worn to samagams, functions and gurdwara, where a puffer is not worn. Function-date-driven, so date the buy to the calendar, not the temperature.

skuLines.line: Baby bunny suit / hooded woollen romper (0-24 M)
skuLines.examples: BABYZONE woollen romper, Modern Mama, Mini Klub, Babyhug hooded suit
skuLines.notes: Zero substitute on campus and zero tolerance for being out of stock — a staff family with a 6-month-old in a Himachal January is not driving 40 km for a bunny suit. Small money, high goodwill.

skuLines.examples: Babyhug newborn 3-pc set, mass hosiery baby sets, hand-knitted local sets
skuLines.seasonality: Oct-Feb, plus year-round gifting for new births on campus
skuLines.notes: Also the default gift when a staff baby is born — sells outside winter too. Hand-knitted local sets carry the best margin and can be sourced from women on or near campus.

skuLines.line: Baby fleece hooded jacket + pant set / blanket-wrap
skuLines.examples: Babyhug fleece set, mass baby fleece 2-pc, Bhuttico kids poncho
skuLines.notes: Fleece over wool for infants — washes daily, dries in a damp hill room, no itch complaint.

skuLines.examples: Monte Carlo kids & men caps, mass acrylic beanie, Zero Degree beanie
skuLines.notes: Highest-margin, lowest-risk line in the category: free size, no size curve, no fashion risk, tiny cube. But read the campus — a turbaned boy or man cannot wear a pull-on cap over a dastaar or patka, so cap demand here is mainly small children, women, non-Sikh staff, and boys before they tie a patka. Do not size the buy off headcount.

skuLines.examples: Unisex monkey cap (mass), Zero Degree monkey cap, local acrylic
skuLines.notes: Unglamorous and it sells out every January. Elderly residents and small children at 6 a.m. prayers are the buyers.

skuLines.examples: Penyan foldable earmuffs, plush ear warmers, knitted ear band
skuLines.notes: The item that actually fits this population: an ear band or earmuff goes over or around a turban where a cap cannot. Stock it deeper than beanies for the male cohort and in plain dark colours for boys, cute/fur for small girls.

skuLines.line: Himachali cap — Kullu / Bushehri / Malana style
skuLines.examples: Bhuttico Himachali cap (Kullu traditional, Bushehri, Malana), Kullu co-op caps
skuLines.seasonality: Oct-Feb; spikes at functions, Himachal Day and for visitor gifting
skuLines.marginBand: 25-35% from a Kullu co-op; better against a direct weaver indent
skuLines.notes: Local identity item, worn by Himachali staff and bought as a gift for visiting parents and dignitaries — the one line a Delhi-catalogue buyer would never think to stock in Sirmaur. Also the cleanest gifting price point in the store.

skuLines.examples: Tahiro woollen gloves, Monte Carlo blend/pure wool gloves, KC Store hand-knitted
skuLines.notes: Lost constantly by boarders, so it re-purchases within a season — treat it as a consumable, not a durable. Stock kids sizes deep; adult free size covers the rest.

skuLines.examples: SUNSHOPPING snow-and-wind-proof gloves, PENYAN bike gloves, Wildcraft, Decathlon
skuLines.seasonality: Nov-Feb, and again in the monsoon for two-wheeler riders
skuLines.notes: For anyone riding a two-wheeler on wet hill road, and for maintenance/estate staff working outdoors. Knitted wool is useless when wet; this is a different product, not an upgrade.

skuLines.examples: HF LUMEN muffler pack-of-3, KRIP KROP, VANTAR, Bhuttico cashmilon muffler
skuLines.notes: For a turbaned wearer the muffler replaces the cap entirely — wrapped over the dastaar and around the ears. That makes it the single most important accessory in this specific store, and multi-packs are the value play.

skuLines.line: Muffler / scarf, pure wool or merino (premium & gifting)
skuLines.examples: Monte Carlo pure-wool muffler, Bhuttico merino/kinnauri muffler, Duke muffler
skuLines.seasonality: Nov-Jan; gifting at functions and farewells
skuLines.notes: Keep the Kinnauri end (₹5,000-24,000) on consignment or by order only — beautiful, but it is a gifting SKU, not stock for a 5,000-person campus store.

skuLines.examples: Bhuttico merino & polywool stoles, mass acrylic stole, Kullu patti stole
skuLines.notes: A woollen stole replaces the cotton chunni for four months — every girl and woman on campus needs one or two, which makes it a far bigger line here than in a metro store. School-permitted colours for the student cohort.

skuLines.line: Men's shawl / loi (staff, elders, gurdwara wear)
skuLines.examples: Vrinde & KAVIM woollen men's shawls, Bhuttico men's Kullu loi (merino/polywool)
skuLines.seasonality: Oct-Feb; gurdwara and samagam use through the season
skuLines.notes: Worn daily over a kurta and to the gurdwara — the culturally correct outer layer for older men here, where a jacket is not worn. Plain white, cream, grey and charcoal cover nearly all demand.

skuLines.line: Women's shawl / chaddar, acrylic or polywool (mass)
skuLines.examples: Bravezi, Goodluck, Varun Cloth House shawls, Bhuttico polywool Kullu shawl
skuLines.notes: The commonest single warm garment for women here — cheaper than a coat, fits over anything, no size. Deep in dark plains and small checks; the printed/embroidered end is slow.

skuLines.line: Kullu / Kinnauri handwoven shawl & pattu (premium local)
skuLines.examples: Bhuttico handwoven merino Kullu shawl, Kullu patti border shawl, Kullu pattu, pashmina loi
skuLines.priceBand: ₹1,650-5,000 merino Kullu shawl; ₹9,500 pashmina loi; ₹15,000-23,500 pattu
skuLines.seasonality: Wedding and function dates, Oct-Feb; visitor gifting year-round
skuLines.marginBand: 20-30% (co-op price lists are tight); 30-40% on a direct weaver indent
skuLines.notes: Consignment or made-to-order only. The pattu at ₹15,000-23,500 is a bridal/occasion piece — hold one or two as display and sell the rest from a catalogue. Genuine local sourcing (Kullu co-ops are ~250 km away) also gives the store a story the residents value.

skuLines.examples: RC Royal Class woollen thumb socks, Texlon, HF LUMEN terry wool, Bhuttico cashmilon socks
skuLines.notes: The most frequently repurchased line in the category — socks are lost, worn through and bought again inside one season. Multi-packs, free size, no colour risk: buy this deep and early. Hand-knitted Lahauli/merino at ₹600 sells to a small premium group.

skuLines.line: School / uniform socks, calf-length in uniform colour
skuLines.examples: Jockey kids socks, Duke calf-length socks, uniform-colour woollen/terry socks
skuLines.packSizes: packs of 3/6 pairs; kids sizes by shoe size
skuLines.notes: Uniform colour and length are fixed by the Academy, and boarders lose pairs weekly — the highest-frequency SKU in the entire winter lane. Never let this stock out between October and February.

skuLines.line: Thermal / cushioned sports socks & inner cotton socks
skuLines.examples: Jockey terry ankle socks, Duke Urban calf socks, mass thermal sports socks
skuLines.notes: Worn as a thin liner under a woollen sock in deep cold, and as games kit the rest of the year. Longer season than anything else on the sock rack.

skuLines.line: Knee caps / leg warmers (woollen, elastic support)
skuLines.examples: Penyan woollen knee cap, Fashiol knee warmer, Infispace leg warmer, thigh-high wool socks
skuLines.seasonality: Nov-Feb; the deep-cold weeks drive nearly all of it
skuLines.notes: Joint pain in a hill winter is the driver, and this is a pharmacy-adjacent purchase the elderly cohort will otherwise do without. Tiny cube, strong margin, and almost never stocked in an apparel assortment.

skuLines.examples: Magic scarf tube, neck gaiter multi-pack, fleece neck warmer
skuLines.seasonality: Dec-Feb; two-wheeler riders and early-morning duty
skuLines.notes: Fits under a turban line and over the ears, and doubles as a dust/rain cover on a two-wheeler. Free size, no risk.

skuLines.examples: Vardhman/Oswal knitting wool, Jyoti circular & straight needles, crochet hooks
skuLines.priceBand: ₹90-250 per 100 g ball; ₹80-300 per needle set
skuLines.seasonality: Aug-Dec — knitting starts well before the cold
skuLines.notes: Hill households still knit their own caps, socks and baby sets, and the season for wool starts two months before the season for sweaters. This is the one line here whose demand you can see coming, and it is a general-store staple that apparel buyers systematically forget.

trends2026: Puffer/quilted is the default winter silhouette in Indian mid-market, and the 2026 spec is a detachable hood — Monte Carlo's current men's puffer run (₹2,337-3,570) is almost entirely 'detachable hood' or 'mock neck', and Duke's jacket line is bomber/puffer-led at ₹1,247-2,622.

Battery-heated jackets have crossed from novelty into mainstream Indian mid-price retail: Monte Carlo is running a live heated-jacket line at ₹2,088-4,074 including boys' sizes — a year ago this was a ₹15,000 adventure-brand item (Royal Enfield's -15°C Adventurer XT, ₹15,950).

Thermals are shifting from bulky waffle cotton to thin merino / 'HeatTech'-style engineered base layers with anti-microbial finishes (Jockey's StayFresh treatment across its winter range) — same warmth, no bulk, and it is what the 18-25 cohort will actually wear.

Reversible and 2-in-1 outerwear is a real 2026 line rather than a gimmick — Duke is carrying reversible jackets and even reversible sweaters (₹1,247-3,436) — pitched as two garments for one price, which also halves a retailer's colour-depth problem.

Oversized hoodies, winter co-ord sets and 'athleisure-winter' have collapsed the line between loungewear and outerwear (Jockey's athleisure-winter block ₹699-2,069; Monte Carlo winter tracksuits) — co-ord sets were called out as the staple of 2026 in mainstream Indian coverage.

Fleece-lined bottoms are the fastest-growing women's winter line in India — fleece leggings, jeggings, fleece night suits and fleece kurti-pyjama sets at ₹300-750 are displacing the traditional thermal lower.

Quick commerce has taken the impulse end of winter: thermals, caps, gloves, socks and mufflers now sit in 10-minute grocery baskets on Blinkit/Zepto/Instamart, which trains buyers to expect warmth on demand — a closed campus 30-50 km from a market is the exact opposite situation, and the store inherits that expectation.

Handloom hill woollens are being repositioned as premium gifting with a full price ladder — the Kullu weavers' co-op now sells ₹450 Himachali caps through ₹1,650-5,000 merino Kullu shawls, ₹9,500 pashmina loi and ₹15,000-23,500 pattu online, so local provenance is a margin story, not just a craft one.

Growth in Indian apparel is being led by value fashion and tier-2/non-metro demand (India Ratings sees double-digit apparel-retailer growth in FY27 on a tier-2 surge; Myntra reports 45% of demand from non-metros), which means the ₹300-900 band, not the ₹3,000 band, is where the volume actually is.
adjacentServices: Alteration and tailoring counter — sleeve/length shortening for growing children, salwar and kurti stitching from unstitched wool-blend suit lengths (the unstitched line does not sell without it)
Name-tape stitching and embroidery on uniform sweaters, cardigans and jackets — boarders lose garments constantly and every house parent asks for it
Pre-season size-set indent for hostel wardens and house parents: booked size curves per house in Aug-Sep, delivered Oct, which converts guesswork into a firm order
A two-week size-exchange window at season open — residents cannot drive 30-50 km to swap a size, so an on-campus exchange is the substitute for a returns policy
Salary-deduction or instalment credit for high-ticket jackets and coats (₹2,000+) against staff payroll
Woollen dry-cleaning / laundry collection plus mothproofed off-season storage of jackets, shawls and blankets
Darning, re-knitting, zip and button repair — extends a hostel sweater by a season and pulls repeat footfall in the dead months
Hand-knitting wool and needles counter with pattern help, feeding the households that knit their own caps, socks and baby sets
Loan/rental pool of heavy jackets and gloves for winter camps, treks and outdoor duty, so nobody buys a ₹3,000 jacket for one trip
End-of-season clearance in Feb-Mar paired with a garment-donation drive, which clears carry-over stock and serves the institution's own charitable mandate
Remote ordering for parents off-campus: order by phone, delivered to the child's hostel with a size-exchange guarantee
